title: two red integration tests: todo_reason and the non-convergence guard
mainwork:
Two integration tests in the iterapp engine's own suite (tests/e2e.rs, which drives a real engine against a fake `claude`) are red on the committed main branch. Both are about a guard telling a human WHY it parked an item — the webapp draws a different chip for each kind of ToDo, and it can only do that if the engine stamps the reason. Neither failure is caused by the change that found them (an unrelated webapp lightbox item); both were verified failing in a clean git worktree at commit 6cf77ff.

CHECK FIRST — this may already be fixed. The working tree was mid-edit in exactly this area when the item was filed (tests/e2e.rs, scheduler.rs, workitems.rs all had uncommitted changes, and the preceding commit was "question state, codepath validation, lock visibility, and stale-lock recovery"). Run both tests before touching anything. If they are green, report the item stale and stop — do not invent work.

The two failures:

- `codepath_guards_and_matching_short_ids` — asserts an item parked by a broken-codepath guard carries `todo_reason: "config"`, with the message "so the UI can tell this from an approval gate". It gets `Null` instead. The engine is parking the item but not recording why, so the webapp's three kinds of ToDo (approval gate / guard park / broken configuration, the 2026-08-26 issue 7b work) collapse into one indistinguishable chip.
- `third_plan_for_same_testgroup_is_held_todo_by_nonconvergence_guard` — asserts the non-convergence guard "announces itself" when it holds the third plan born from the same testgroup. The item's text instead carries only the whole-tree codepath-lock warning and the automation-override note; the non-convergence announcement is missing. A human reviewing that held item is not told it was the third lap around the same red testgroup, which is the one fact that explains why it is sitting there.

Decide per failure whether the ENGINE stopped stamping the reason or the TEST is asserting something the design moved away from, and fix whichever is actually wrong — do not silence a test to make it green. If the answer is that the design changed deliberately, update the test AND say so explicitly in your output.

Acceptance: `cargo test` passes whole (180 unit tests in the binary plus all 32 in tests/e2e.rs). Finish with `cargo build --release` — deploys copy from target/release/.

Agent-level detail — the exact reproduction:

    cd /Users/stephen.hilton/dev/iterapp
    cargo test --test e2e codepath_guards_and_matching_short_ids
    cargo test --test e2e third_plan_for_same_testgroup_is_held_todo_by_nonconvergence_guard

First panics with: assertion `left == right` failed: so the UI can tell this from an approval gate / left: Null / right: "config".
Second panics with: guard announces itself: <the codepath whole-tree warning>, note: state "queued" overridden to "todo" — the automation mode (review, inherited default) decides how agent-created items are born.

This project has no `*.testgroup.iter.md` files, so there is no `iter runtests` group to claim against; `cargo test` is the deterministic runner here.
